LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. Last weekend against the Cleveland Browns, things got as bad as we've seen this season , as the Texans were called for a season-high 13 penalties and 112 yards. Impressively enough, four of those penalties were caused because of their special teams unit. Could the Texans magically turn a corner in this game and look like a more disciplined, refined unit to limit the penalties? It's always possible. Maybe the solution to those penalty problems finally clicked for DeMeco Ryans and this coaching staff after the events of last weekend. These teams are in two different places in 2026, yet they both only have three wins through the first 10 weeks of the season. Indianapolis traded away several key players at the deadline, including Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, DeForest Buckner, and Quenton Nelson, as the team simply doesn't have the same juice that it did to open the 2025 campaign. Despite that, the Colts have a win over Houston in 2026, and the Texans have struggled against just about everyone this season. Houston is 3-6 through nine games, losing on the road against the Cleveland Browns in Week 10. The Texans blew a 17-0 lead in that matchup, struggling mightily on offense in the second half. While C.J. Stroud has played well in the 2026 season, the Houston defense has not lived up to expectations after it finished No. 1 in EPA/Play during the 2025 campaign. Oddsmakers still have the Texans favored by 12.5 points at home in this AFC South battle. Can Houston get back on track and keep its slim playoff hopes alive? A win on Thursday would go a long way to getting the Texans back in the mix for the No. 7 seed in the AFC. Here's a breakdown of some of our favorites to get you ready to bet on the first primetime matchup in Week 11 of the NFL season. Instead, I'm going to take the OVER. The Texans' offense has been their strength this season. They're now ninth in the league in EPA per play and fourth in that metric since Week 4. C.J. Stroud has also been phenomenal, ranking inside the top eight in almost every quarterback metric since Week 4. Now they'll get to feast against a horrific Colts defense that's 21st in opponent EPA per play. Of course, it's hard to trust the Colts' offense, but it's time for us to continue to assume that the Houston offense is going to turn things around and become the elite unit it was the past few seasons. The biggest red flag in this game is that they're 22nd in opponent rush EPA and 27th in opponent rush success rate, which will feed directly into the Colts' offensive strength with Jonathan Taylor. Jonathan Taylor has seen his snap share dip a bit in recent weeks – playing less than 70 percent of the offensive plays in four games in a row – yet he’s still handled a ton of touches for Indy. Taylor carried the ball 13 times for 46 yards in Week 9 against Dallas and 16 times for 83 yards in Week 10 against Miami. He had 23 carries and cleared this prop in Week 3 against Houston, which is 20th in EPA/Rush and allowing 4.0 yards per carry this season. The Colts star has at least 50 rushing yards in seven of his 10 games this season, picking up at least 45 rushing yards in nine of his games. Taylor is still the safest bet to go off for an Indy team that moved on from both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline. Houston wideout Nico Collins has found the end zone in back-to-back weeks, and he has five touchdowns in seven appearances in the 2026 season. The clear No. 1 option for this Houston offense through the air, Collins has already seen 55 targets from C.J. Stroud, reeling in 37 of them for 478 yards. He was targeted 16 times in the loss to Cleveland in Week 10, and with the Houston running game struggling in 2026, I expect the offense to rely on Stroud throwing the ball on Thursday. The Colts have allowed 17 passing touchdowns this season, but Collins missed the first meeting against them with an injury. I think he makes his presence felt on Thursday night and scores for the third game in a row. After missing all of last season and the start of the 2026 season recovering from a brutal knee injury, Tank Dell is back – and thriving – with Stroud at quarterback. Dell and Stroud have some great chemistry in their time together in the NFL, and the young receiver has played just under 50 percent of the offensive snaps in back-to-back weeks. In Week 9, Dell had four grabs for 105 yards and a score, receiving nine targets from Stroud. He then followed that up with a three-catch game (on four targets) against Cleveland. Dell isn’t going to lead this receiver room in snaps, but he’s getting looks from Stroud when he’s out there and is now facing a defense that is 18th in EPA/Pass, allowing the sixth-most passing yards in the league. picks.blurb: Houston Texans vs Indianapolis Colts: Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Vikings-49ers live updates Tarik Skubal to Mets NFL Week 11 Winners-Losers Tom Jackson dies College football winners/losers Houston Texans vs Indianapolis Colts: Predictions HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 17: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans runs withe ball during the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at NRG Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Bob Levey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mike Bullock · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 3:01 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Here we have 2 teams both racing for the basement – the 3-7 Indianapolis Colts and the 3-6 Houston Texans. The Colts traded away most of their key players to start a rebuild, while the Texans trotted out a failed offensive scheme and altered the winning defensive scheme from 2025. 1 team wants to lose, the other wants to win – but loses anyway. The baby horses currently lead the all-time series, 33-15-1 thanks in great part to the Peyton Manning/Marvin Harrison Sr. years. However, Houston has won 5 of past 6, thanks to the Colts no longer showing interest in winning football. On paper, as of this writing, the Texans should absolutely dominate this game – and very well may. H-Town QB C.J. Stroud is having an MVP season. The Houston wide receiver corps is one of the best in the league – including the son of the aforementioned Harrison Sr.. Their run game ran away when Joe Mixon suffered the mystery of the ages injury in 2024, but Stroud has still managed to find ways to complete 201 passes for 2462 yards, 19 touchdowns and only 3 INTs. The offensive line remains offensive, mostly, but has had just enough get-in-the-way-ness to give Stroud time to throw. Currently, the Texans passing attack is 4th overall. Defensively, Houston has the horsepower to compete at an elite level, but due to off-coverage, injuries and what looks to be confusion with the gameplan, they're currently ranked 20th. Some believe it's a little too much "read your own press coverage", others blame coaching and play calling. In some ways it seems a desire to change up from last season to keep opponents guessing has taken this defense away from what they do best. If you're great at zigging, but decide to zag all the time cause you think your opponent is expecting the zig, then you need to be ok with ignoring your own strengths… We won't talk about the special teams… #ulcerinducing Meanwhile, over in the baby horse stable, the Colts are clearly trotting down the rebuild trail. So far in 2026 Indy has: A new owner who has taken direct control over the coaching staff An interim general manager (after firing their previous one late last month) Quenton Nelson: Traded to the Seattle Seahawks. DeForest Buckner: Traded to the San Francisco 49ers. Josh Downs: Traded to the Kansas City Chiefs. Keenan Allen: Traded to the San Francisco 49ers. And managed to win 1 game since all these team-affecting moves. Their current goal seems to be the #1 draft pick, if the Los Angeles Chargers don't beat them to it. Colts vs Texans predictions: In true Houston Texans fashion, the Texans will beat an opponent who doesn't want to win. Just as they did to the aforementioned Chargers. The 2026 brand of Texans football doesn't defeat winning teams (exception: the Jacksonville Jaguars cause, #Glitter). They do, however, lose the battle to not win – meaning when an opponent wants to lose, they freely allow H-Town to go to town on them. Which will happen again tonight. Stroud will look like an MVP candidate on a national stage. The Colts will show all their dysfunction. And the talking heads will ignore the apparent incoming mutiny on Kirby Drive. Indianapolis Colts 13 Houston Texans 38 Those with a superficial knowledge of the Texans will beat the drum that they still have a shot at the playoffs, and how they've fixed their issues. Until the following week when they lose against the Baltimore Ravens at the end of the month. Meanwhile, those who do lift the hood and look beyond the check engine light glaring on this franchise's dashboard will see a different prediction: The end game pot is on the stove, simmering away. Chances are tonight will turn the burn down just long enough to have a nice Thanksgiving.

away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

Coming off a disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints continue to struggle with offensive consistency and finishing games under head coach Kellen Moore. Those problems could prove costly against a well-rounded Chicago team that boasts one of the NFL's most productive offenses and a top-10 defense. Can the Saints pull off an unlikely upset, or will their struggles continue against one of the NFC's top contenders? Here's how our staff predicts Sunday's matchup will unfold. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 28-14 This is a game that doesn’t favor the Saints. The Bears are by far the best team the Saints have faced since the Detroit Lions , who beat New Orleans in overtime. They have one of the league’s best offenses , led by quarterback Caleb Williams , and one of the league's most balanced teams. Defensively, the Bears have a top-10 defense. Chicago boasts a top-10 defense, ranking eighth in scoring (20.4 PPG) and seventh in total defense (310.9 YPG). Their strength lies against the run, allowing 91.1 yards per game (seventh-fewest), while placing 15th against the pass (219.8 YPG). Crucially, the Bears lead the NFL in third-down defense (22.8% conversion rate allowed) and rank 12th in red-zone touchdown efficiency (53.8%). They maintain consistent pass pressure with 26 sacks (ninth) and seven interceptions (tied for 11th). Also, this will be the first cold-weather game for the Saints as the temperature will be in the 50s throughout the game. I don’t think the Saints will pull off the upset, but what I do know is that the Saints have played better on the road as both of their wins came on the road against the Baltimore Ravens and New York Giants . I do think its defense will do enough to make this game tight before Chicago pulls away near the end. Prediction : Bears 28 Saints 14 Doug Joubert, Publisher: L 32-21 This is a Saints team that seems to be searching, searching for an identity, a consistent offense, people on the same page. The New Orleans offense sputters and coughs more than my old 1969 VW Beetle. No matter what I would do to that little air-cooled engine, it never could quite get started, and when it did, it usually took a few minutes of driving before it would get going smoothly. Once it was warmed up, that little thing was a joy to drive. Unfortunately, it took a while to even get to that point. The Saints O reminds me of that Beetle. They can't seem to get going in the beginning. Once they get warmed up and going, they are fun to watch. Until then, it's almost torturous to be a part of. Eventually, I had to get rid of that little car. Keeping the valves aligned properly on that rapidly expanding air-cooled engine proved to be one of those "I'll be doing this forever" kind of projects, so I just gave up and moved on. The New Orleans offense is at that point, in my opinion. A squad that cannot consistently move the ball, stopping and starting itself with poor run blocking, or wide receivers and a quarterback who aren't on the same page, or play calling that comes across as vanilla as can be (think runs in the middle). Now, Brandon Staley's group is another story, another car if you will. They remind me of a Tesla. The Saints defense can really get going with the first acceleration, but fade at the end. A battery-powered Tesla is a lot like that. They can fly right out the gate and tear the street up, but don't expect that to last, as those batteries won't go 300-plus miles (no matter what they say) like a gas-power engine will, losing energy much sooner than their gas counterparts. This Saints defense has produced through the first three quarters, especially for the last few games. Although getting turnovers has been a notable absence for this group, it has played well, up until the final quarter. To wit, the Panthers' game. I say all that to say this: you cannot do any of what the offense and defense has been doing against a quality team. The Panthers, Browns, and Steelers were not quality teams. This Bears team is. It will take a complete game, start to finish, for this Saints team to have a chance to beat Chicago. The local boys haven't done that all year long. away.headline: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears
away.blurb: Sheesh. The New Orleans Saints (3-6) shared a lengthy injury report ahead of Sunday's game with the Chicago Bears (7-2), with seven players not participating and two other limited to start the week. They'll need all hands on deck for a chance at upsetting one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Let's hope they can get it done. And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Donaldson has been a productive rusher for New Orleans on limited snaps (averaging 4.8 yards per carry and a team-high 64.7% success rate), and he was just starting to earn a bigger role after initially getting on the field as a short-yardage specialist. He competes hard in pass protection, too. How snaps could be divided between him, Travis Etienne Jr., Alvin Kamara (more on him in a minute), and Audric Estime remains to be seen. What about those seven players who didn't practice? We expected Kamara (not injury related) would get his usual rest day, which has been a pattern since he suffered a Week 5 back injury. He turned 31 this summer and has worn a lot of tread off his tires so it makes sense to give him a lighter workload during the week, especially if he's going to have a reduced role on game days. Kamara was only on the field last Sunday for 16 snaps but he scored two touchdowns. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) did not practice on Wednesday due to a personal matter, and head coach Kellen Moore was noncommittal when asked if Reid was expected back on Thursday. Stay tuned. Backup right tackle Asim Richards (knee) and a couple of defensive starters who got nicked up against the Carolina Panthers -- cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) -- were held out of practice. Additionally, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) and center Erik McCoy (biceps) both did not practice, though Moore said "we'll see" if either of them can return to work later this week. Two other players were limited to start the week: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest), who you can read more about here ; and backup corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh). We'll be watching for updates on their status as the week continues. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears

home.blurb: Chicago is in good position coming off its bye week, as RB Kyle Monangai has been cleared to play after missing more than a month due to thumb and toe injuries. Additionally, DL Jeffery Simmons had no designation on Friday's injury report after being limited on Thursday due to a knee issue, so he's good to go. Meanwhile, Gordon was already ruled out for Sunday's game with a shoulder injury, while WR/returner Zavion Thomas was listed as questionable on Friday's injury report with an ankle injury. Thomas was not on the list of inactives, so he's presumably set to go Sunday. New Orleans' Friday injury report was more lengthy, with Emerson (concussion), Fuaga (knee), McCoy (biceps), DB Justin Reid (personal) and Richards (knee) already ruled out for Sunday's game and DB Decamerlon Richardson (chest) and LB Pete Werner (hamstring) listed as questionable. Werner is out Sunday, while Richardson is presumably good to go. LAKE FOREST, Ill. (AP/ WGN ) — Carl Granderson and Chase Young form a potent 1-2 punch on defense for the New Orleans Saints. Jeffery Simmons is a force on the defensive line for the Chicago Bears. Granderson and Young are two of the biggest concerns for Chicago coach Ben Johnson going into Sunday's game against New Orleans. Same goes for Saints coach Kellen Moore and Simmons. “They’re good, not just only in the pass game, they’re great edge setters in the run game as well,” Johnson said. “So big challenge there on both sides.” Granderson has a team-high 8 1/2 sacks in eight games in his eighth season with New Orleans, matching his career high set in the 2023 season. He had one of the Saints' three sacks in last Sunday's 20-17 loss to Carolina. Young has eight sacks in nine games in his third year with New Orleans after a career-best 10 sacks last season. Granderson and Young are a potent outside duo, and Kaden Elliss also contributes to the pass rush. He had a team-high 15 tackles and a sack against the Panthers. “I think he’s one of the better pressuring linebackers in the NFL,” Johnson said. "And so, they’re not afraid to plug him in A or B gap and make it tough on your protection scheme. That combination, I think, from the interior with him with those two edge rushers is what makes their pressure package so dangerous.” Chicago, meanwhile, returns from its bye week with a four-game winning streak, helped by the acquisition of Simmons in a blockbuster trade with Tennessee on Oct. 29. The All-Pro defensive tackle has one sack in each of his first two games with his new team. Beyond his pass-rushing abilities, Simmons also has made life easier on Chicago's linebackers and defensive ends through the attention he demands up front. “He’s one of the top interior defensive linemen in the league," Moore said. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. away.headline: Report: Titans pass rusher involved in severe vehicle incident before Week 11 showdown
away.source: Last Word On Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Reports emerged on Saturday afternoon that an injured Tennessee Titans pass rusher was involved in a serious vehicle accident. Initial reports indicated that Jaylen Harrell was involved in the accident and was hospitalized with injuries. However, later reporting that Harrell’s level of involvement escalated into potential assault. Report: Titans Pass Rusher Involved In Severe Vehicle Incident Before Week 11 Showdown Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the allegations against the Titans pass rusher involved in the accident, so nothing substantive can be said yet. This is the third serious incident involving a Titans player in recent months. Calvin Ridley allegedly committed assault in Nashville, and Jordan Elliott was released after attempting to retrieve a firearm following an altercation with OT J.C. Latham. Ridley’s case is still being adjudicated, while Elliott landed another tryout opportunity with the Chicago Bears. The Titans released a boilerplate statement wishing Harrell and his family well after the accident, but revealed nothing before the seriousness of the allegations emerged. Now that the allegations are public, the league office and the franchise must do their due diligence. The Titans pass rusher has imperiled his career if these are ultimately proven true. This is the first known off-field incident that Harrell has been involved in since he entered the NFL as a seventh-round selection in the 2024 draft. Harrell landed on injured reserve during the 2026 preseason with an ACL injury, ending his season before it began. In two seasons, he has produced 38 tackles, seven tackles for loss, and 4.5 sacks as a key reserve for the Titans. He was expected to contribute meaningful reps as a backup in 2026, but the injury made it impossible. The allegations are serious enough to warrant a further look by the franchise and league, as the Titans pass rusher involved himself to a degree that a second car was part of the incident. He allegedly assaulted the driver from the backseat, which caused the original vehicle to hit a second one and resulted in damage to a light pole in the end. As a result of the accident, Harrell was thrown forward against the windshield with enough force to require hospitalization. If he is found guilty of what is alleged, jail time is certainly on the table. Financially, the Titans would take a dead cap hit of $ 1,190,000 if he is released during the 2027 offseason, with cap savings of $20,184. It isn’t a huge number that could affect signings in the near future, but a mere rounding error on the cap sheet. As a former seventh-round selection still on his rookie contract, Harrell’s contract is a pittance to absorb easily. More than likely, he will get suspended and/or cut once the authorities, league, and the franchise complete the investigation. The Titans pass rusher involved in the accident could see his aspiring career end before it really could ascend into meaningful reps, due to his own doing. Harre

home.blurb: Both teams have struggled defensively, but the Cowboys' issues against the run could allow Tennessee to continue its recent positive offensive trajectory. Here are six intriguing storylines heading into Sunday's matchup at AT&T Stadium. 1. Both teams are coming off high-scoring losses High-scoring affairs have become a staple for the Cowboys this season, as they have played four games with a final score of both teams scoring 30 or more points. The highest of those games was their 46-40 loss to the 49ers last Sunday. Meanwhile, the Titans surrendered 40 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars in a 40-23 loss, marking the second consecutive game in which Tennessee allowed at least 40 points. Their defense also gave up 43 points in its overtime loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. Those results highlight a potential opportunity for a shootout on Sunday. For Tennessee, the challenge will be finding a way to slow down a Dallas offense that has demonstrated its ability to score against several opposing defenses all season long. 2. The Cowboys have the NFL's worst run defense One of the biggest advantages Tennessee could have entering Sunday's matchup is the Cowboys' struggles against the run. They rank last in the NFL in rushing defense, allowing 154.1 yards per game. That creates an appealing matchup for a Titans rushing attack that has shown signs of improvement in recent weeks against other weak run defenses. The Titans also averaged a season-best 6.2 yards per carry collectively against Jacksonville in Week 10. Despite his success rushing for over 1000 yards in back-to-back seasons, the Titans prioritized Pollard more than Dallas during his free agency in 2024. Pollard has continued producing in Nashville, recording two additional 1000+ yard seasons and is on pace for his fifth straight year of achieving it with 628 rushing yards through nine games this season. They're well-rested off their bye week, but they're set to face off against a strong 7-2 Detroit Lions team on the road in what could be the toughest remaining game on the schedule. The Bucs themselves are 3-6, but despite that, they remain one game back from the NFC South lead. The defense has been elite and the run game has been stout, but the passing offense has been a big problem for Tampa Bay — and it may not get much better, as quarterback Baker Mayfield is set to play this game while dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury. As always, we've rounded up our staff to lock in our picks for Sunday's game. Can the Bucs pull off the upset? Or will they fall to 3-7? Caleb Skinner, Writer: Lions 20, Bucs 17 It's getting to the point for the Bucs that they must win, or their season could be over. And things don't get easier this week as they take on the Lions. The Lions own one of the NFL's elite offenses and will test the Bucs' top-rated defense. It's unlikely they'll replicate their turnover margin as they did against the Bears, but they can most definitely slow Detroit down. While the defense won't be too much of a worry, the problems will once again come on the offensive side of the ball for Tampa Bay. The Lions' defense has stepped it up in recent weeks, and even without Aidan Hutchinson, they should be able to stymie the offense enough. I expect this one to be a low-scoring affair at Ford Field, with the Lions coming away with a close home victory to drop the Bucs to 3-7 on the year. Overall Record: 5-4 James Hill, Writer: Lions 24, Bucs 17 Baker Mayfield is once again on the mend from an injury. Yes, the Lions have injuries of their own with Aiden Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, but I don’t know if a hobbled Baker Mayfield or a healthy Jalon Daniels will be able to get the job done. Overall Record: 4-5 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Lions 27, Bucs 21 As much as I believe that the Buccaneers' defense is for real, I also believe the offense is not. Detroit, on the other hand, has one of the most dynamic offenses in the entire league. Beyond just the litany of weapons he has at his disposal, Jared Goff has been extremely effective playing against Bowles' blitz-heavy defenses over the past several years. For the Bucs to win, they'll need to get pressure with four to avoid sending extra guys to disrupt Goff in the pocket. The problem is, even if they do that and manage to generate turnovers like they have been so far this year on defense, the Bucs will need Baker Mayfield to look like a competent NFL QB on offense to win this football game. Sadly, I'm not sure if that version of Mayfield even exists anymore. Overall Record: 6-3 Logan Robinson, Founder: Lions 27, Bucs 20 Another battle for Todd Bowles against a high-scoring offense in Detroit. I’m excited to watch that, but the next thing I’m most intrigued about is the Bucs’ offensive passing attack. That has to improve, or Tampa Bay isn’t making the playoffs — It’s quite simple for me on that. Hopefully the bye week helped, but I’m very cautious about picking the Buccaneers. River Wells, Editor: Lions 24, Bucs 16 The Bucs have a few things going for them, but this is a passing league, and unfortunately, they don't have the passing offense to hang with good teams — much less an elite one like the Lions. The defense will likely hold the Detroit Lions' dynamic offense in check, but the passing offense won't be enough, and it could be even worse than usual with Mayfield's injury. I think the Bucs defense will keep them in it, but it won't be enough to win against a team that could end up winning the brutal NFC North this season. Consensus: Lions 5, Bucs 0 Once again, our staff isn't picking Tampa Bay whatsoever. Our staff unanimously picked the Bears two weeks ago, and we've unanimously picked the Lions here. It's any given Sunday in the NFL, so the Bucs are always in it. But they'll have to convince us that they can beat good teams, and so far, they simply haven't. picks.blurb: Roundtable: Lions Week 11 Preview Against Buccaneers Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Detroit Lions Week 11 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. 1. How much is Aidan Hutchinson to blame for his ACL injury? Christian Booher: I think Hutchinson is definitely deserving of some blame for the fact that the injury occurred in such an unnecessary fashion. The movements that went into that injury have been analyzed, and it's rightfully pointed out that a move like the one he did to celebrate that sack poses a risk. However, it's such a fluke situation that it's hard to be extremely mad at the circumstances. He's done that celebration many times, and it just so happens that he has to learn of the risks this way. Vito Chirco: At the end of the day, it was a freak accident and could've happened to any one of the hundreds of players that celebrate after sacks and other big plays. However, as a defensive captain and veteran player now, he should've known better than to leave his feet to celebrate, especially after his previous season-ending injury just two years ago. Consequently, I believe it's fair to say that Hutchinson deserves to shoulder a fair portion of the blame for the ACL ailment. Emmett Matasovsky: It was not the smartest play by Aidan Hutchinson in that injury, I cannot lie. That said, the amount of negative comments towards the EDGE is a bit extreme this week. When a play like that happens, most players’ ligaments tend to be a few plays from giving during game action, frankly. It was not a smart celebration, especially with previous comments to stop the celebrations that could cause non-contact injuries. I will say it is a 60 percent Hutchinson fault, 40 percent circumstance of being close to a natural injury anyway. 2. Are Buccaneers going to be able to slow down Jahmyr Gibbs? Booher : I think the Lions will find some tough sledding on the ground throughout Sunday's game. The Buccaneers have had success against the Lions in past matchups when it comes to slowing down the run game, and with Vita Vea leading the charge, I think the Lions will once again struggle to run the ball. As a result, I think the key to victory is the right arm of Jared Goff, as he'll need to keep the offense on schedule through the air. Chirco : Despite the Buccaneers’ prowess against the run this season, I believe that Gibbs still ends up with a solid day on the ground. And you know that Drew Petzing will also deploy the dual-threat runner as often as possible as a receiver. I expect Gibbs to be contained a bit, but to still produce a couple of big runs in the Week 11 contest. Matasovsky : With the Buccaneers battered and the Lions with momentum, the best hope for Tampa Bay is that Gibbs has jetlag. I think it will be tough sledding for the Tampa defensive line. Gibbs has hit his stride and is coming off a performance of over 250 yards from scrimmage. The fatigue, especially post-international travel, might lead to more Vaki touches, but I do not see the Bucs stopping the Lions running backs room. 3. Who will be Detroit Lions game MVP? Booher : I think Goff is the MVP on Sunday. As I mentioned, the Lions could really struggle to run the ball, which puts more pressure on Goff and offensive coordinator Drew Petzing to dial up counters. Another player that I think is due for a big day is tight end Sam LaPorta, who will likely match up with former Detroit defensive standout Alex Anzalone throughout Sunday's game. Chirco : I'm going to go with Alim McNeill. The run-stuffing interior lineman has had an ultra productive campaign thus far this season, and he will need to come up big Sunday against Tampa Bay RB Bucky Irving. He also will be counted upon even more now as a pass-rusher due to the season-ending injury to EDGE Aidan Hutchinson. With all this said, I believe he'll deliver a solid performance against the Buccaneers, keying a sixth straight victory for Detroit. Matasovsky : It would be foolish to not select Gibbs here. Jahmyr Gibbs has a chance to run free and make plays, especially if Yaya Diaby is out. The back will have a phenomenal backing up from his Munich game, with another effort over 100 yards rushing and two total touchdowns. 4. Will Kerby Joseph make a big impact this week? Booher : I'm tempering my expectations for Joseph in his first game of the season. More than anything, I want to see him be pain-free in his return to action. Before he was officially shut down last year, he would often depart games for a series at a time while dealing with this nagging knee injury, and so I want to see him get through the matchup without having to depart due to pain. Chirco : I'm going to say no. I think the All-Pro safety will log 45-50 total defensive snaps in his season debut. But ultimately, I believe he'll show signs of being hampered by his lingering knee issue. I'd temper my expectations from Joseph in this Week 11 matchup. Matasovsky : I can see this going both ways. I could see Kerby Joseph making a huge play, especially against potentially an undrafted rookie quarterback. However, I can also argue that I see Joseph on a “pitch count” and limited reps. Personally, I hope that it is the former, where Joseph announces he is back with an interception and gets his moment to celebrate in front of the home crowd. 5. What do you want to see from DE Ahmed Hassanein in his debut this season? Booher : Hassanein is a player that is easy to root for due to his mentality and his journey to the NFL. It's been a tough road since he was drafted by Detroit last year, but Sunday will be his first chance to prove he belongs. In the big end role that he will likely play, Hassanein needs to be firm in setting the edge, and I think he could also make an impact with a few pressures if he gets opportunities in passing downs. Chirco : I believe it's reasonable to expect Hassanein to garner a couple of QB hits and pressures in his NFL debut on Sunday. He faces a difficult task going up against the slippery Baker Mayfield. However, the Lions will be counting on the Boise State product to make life at least a little bit difficult for the veteran passer. Matasovsky : Hassanein will have a chance to make an impact, but I will settle for the Boise State product at least making a mark on the box score. It is tough to argue that he deserves more reps than a red hot Derrick Moore, who has four sacks in the last two outings. The former Lions sixth-round pick has earned the right to play, and was likely going to get a chance before Hutchinson’s injury prompted the move up the depth chart. That said, now is the time for the Egyptian. I want to see the player do his job and make positive plays, even if it is not a box score-stuffing day. At the end of the day, the second-year pro is a role player, and football is a game where all 11 players doing their job and role means a successful day. Simply put, I want a penalty free, “plus” day from Hassanein. Published 16 hours ago VITO CHIRCO Vito has covered the NFL and the Detroit Lions for the past five years. Has extensive reporting history of college athletics, the Detroit Tigers and Detroit Mercy Athletics. Chirco's work include NFL columns, analyzing potential Detroit Lions prospects coming out of college, NFL draft coverage and analysis of events occurring in the NFL. A trip to Ford Field to face the 7-2 Detroit Lions is a tough place to start fixing that. The quarterback news is better than it looked earlier in the week. Head coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Baker Mayfield is trending in the right direction to start on his sprained foot, according to NBC Sports . Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's noon CT kickoff. 1. Bucky Irving outrushes Jahmyr Gibbs Gibbs leads the NFL with 1,000 rushing yards, and Bowles compared him to Barry Sanders this week. He's also running into the best run defense in the league . Tampa Bay allows 79.1 rushing yards per game, the fewest in the NFL, according to ESPN. We compared each back's average to what the other defense allows. Gibbs averages 111.1 rushing yards per game, about 32 more than the Bucs give up to entire offenses. Irving averages 91.7 per game on 4.9 yards per carry, almost exactly the 90.4 Detroit allows. On paper, Irving has the easier path. 2. Tez Johnson catches a 40-yard pass Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Tez Johnson (15) makes a catch past Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) in the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Johnson has only 11 catches, but he's averaging 23.1 yards per reception with a long of 64, according to ESPN . Nobody else on the roster with more than five catches is close to that average. Detroit is playing without Aidan Hutchinson, and the Lions will have to respect Irving and the run game. One play-action shot to Johnson is the easiest way for a quarterback on a sore foot to change the game without having to move much. 3. The Bucs intercept Jared Goff twice Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers cornerback Jacob Parrish (25) intercepts a pass intended for Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London (5) thrown by quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (not pictured) during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Goff has thrown four interceptions all season, so this one is bold. Tampa Bay has 21 takeaways , and 16 of them are interceptions. Zyon McCollum and Alex Anzalone have four apiece, and Jacob Parrish has two. Parrish draws Amon-Ra St. Brown, and he's PFF's No. 4 cornerback . If Goff keeps feeding St. Brown against Bowles' zone looks, the Bucs will get a couple of chances to jump a route. 4. Tampa Bay wins its first one-score game Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers placekicker Chase McLaughlin (4) celebrates with punter Riley Dixon (9) after kicking a thirty-four-yard field goal against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images The Bucs' three wins came by eight, 30 and 16 points. Every loss has been by seven or fewer, and the red zone is a big reason. Tampa Bay has scored touchdowns on 15 of its 31 trips inside the 20 and settled for field goals on 12 others. That's why this ends with Chase McLaughlin. He's made all 22 of his field-goal attempts this season, and a close game in Detroit finally breaks Tampa Bay's way on his leg. Bucs 23, Lions 21. away.headline: Which Buccaneers stepped up as injuries piled up before the bye?
away.blurb: His involvement was growing before the comparison period ended, reaching a season-high 30 defensive snaps against Carolina in Week 7. Walker's increased playing time is particularly important with Yaya Diaby dealing with a knee injury, although the available reporting does not establish that Walker's entire increase resulted from Diaby's absence. Injuries forced Tampa Bay to adjust before the bye, but the increased playing time also created opportunities to evaluate its depth. Chukwuma and Johnson showed they could contribute when starters were unavailable, while Durham, Sharp, and Walker earned bigger roles that could remain valuable in the second half of the season. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered their Week 10 bye having dealt with injuries at quarterback, wide receiver, offensive tackle, and across the defense. Those absences forced lineup adjustments, but they also gave other players chances to show what they could contribute when called upon to step up. According to DepthRoom's snap-count data , five Buccaneers increased their share of playing time by at least 10 percentage points when comparing Weeks 4–6 with Weeks 7–9. Some stepped in for injured starters, while others saw their roles expand as personnel usage changed. Chukwuma saw the biggest increase, rising from 0% of Tampa Bay's offensive snaps in Weeks 4–6 to 33% over the next three games. His opportunity came when Luke Goedeke missed Week 7 against Carolina with a calf injury. Chukwuma started at right tackle and helped Tampa Bay rush for 258 yards in a 43-13 victory. According to Scott Smith's official team report , it was Chukwuma's third career start, and Todd Bowles expressed confidence in his potential to become a full-time NFL starter. Johnson's snap share climbed from 43% to 62%, with Emeka Egbuka's absence opening a spot at wide receiver. Egbuka missed Weeks 7 and 8 while dealing with concussion and foot injuries. Johnson started against Carolina and played 41 offensive snaps, contributing a 19-yard third-down reception, a 14-yard rushing gain, and a 14-yard touchdown catch. His involvement continued growing after Egbuka returned, reaching 54 snaps, or 79% of the offense, against Chicago in Week 9. Durham increased his offensive snap share from 26% to 46%, becoming a more frequent part of Tampa Bay's tight end rotation. The Buccaneers had already shown a willingness to use multiple tight ends, including opening their Week 6 matchup against Pittsburgh with three on the field. Durham's increase reflects a larger role in those personnel packages, although no specific injury has been established as the reason for his additional playing time. Perhaps the Egubka injury contributed to lineups with more tight ends on the field. Sharp's playing time rose from 6% to 23%, giving the rookie more opportunities alongside Cade Otton and Durham. away.headline: Lions release initial injury report vs. Buccaneers: DJ Reed returns
away.blurb: Starting center Cade Mays (ankle) did not practice. Starting cornerback DJ Reed (hip) returned to practice, but he was a limited participant. Reed has missed each of the Lions' past two games, and the 5-foot-9, 190-pound corner didn't practice either week. Linebacker Joe Bachie (knee), cornerback Khalil Dorsey (ankle), defensive lineman Tyler Lacy (shoulder), cornerback Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder), and running back Sione Vaki (ankle) were also all limited participants. As the Detroit Lions (7-2) gear up for Sunday's showdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6), the team released their initial injury report ahead of the matchup. The Lions activated safety Kerby Joseph on Wednesday. Joseph, who has been working back from a chronic knee injury, was a full participant in the Lions ' initial injury report. home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

home.headline: Bucs-Lions Inactives | Baker Mayfield Will Start
home.blurb: Quarterback Baker Mayfield is dealing with a foot injury but it won't keep him out of Sunday's pivotal contest against the Lions in Detroit…Edge rusher Yaya Diaby is also returning from a knee injury Quarterback Baker Mayfield will suit up for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11 against the Detroit Lions after overcoming a foot injury suffered in Week Nine in Chicago. He was listed as questionable on Friday's injury report after being limited in practice on Thursday and Friday but has been cleared to play on Sunday. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby is also returning to action after missing one game (and the bye week) with a knee injury. However, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. is out due to an ankle injury sustained in the Bears game. Former Lion Ifeatu Melifonwu will start in his place next to Tykee Smith. Will that trend continue in Week 11? Visiting head coach Andy Reid's crew are Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals, who managed to capture two wins in three games earlier this campaign but have since dropped back-to-back outings. Down to their fourth quarterback of the year, their work is cut out for them against a surging Kansas City squad. With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 11 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: In each of the last two weeks, I’ve been able to genuinely argue that the Jets and Falcons were better (or at least more dangerous) than their meager records would indicate. The 3-7 Cardinals are probably worse than their record, especially while they’re preparing to be quarterbacked by a new-in-town 40-year-old super-journeyman. There are no excuses for the Chiefs to stumble in this game. The Chiefs have put up 35 points in each of their last two wins while holding the Jets and Falcons to 12 and 13 points, respectively. With the Buffalo Bills on the horizon, I expect a similarly stout defensive performance, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the Chiefs are content to park the bus offensively if they hold a second-half lead over Arizona. Jordan Foote: Given their recent shellackings of the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons, it's hard not to think the Chiefs will emerge with a comfortable Week 11 victory over the Cardinals here. Arizona is simply too devoid of talent on either side of the ball, leaving only a bizarre outcome that borders on a miracle being the club's main path to a win. Kansas City's banged-up roster is still miles ahead of Arizona's, with the duo of Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson alone being enough to move the chains. On the other side of the ball, Josh Johnson is an experienced vet, but Steve Spagnuolo may have something in store for him. Give me the Chiefs to roll to 8-2 on the year as the toughest part of their schedule approaches. Joshua Schulman: There’s very little meaningful analysis to provide against an opponent of this caliber. The Cardinals are down several key starters and have been one of the NFL's worst teams over the past handful of weeks. With 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson set to fill in for the injured Carson Beck, I’m expecting the Chiefs to steamroll Arizona. Look for Emmett Johnson to have another big game as Kenneth Walker misses his second consecutive game . Tyler Brown: For the third straight week, I think the Chiefs win by three touchdowns. Emmett Johnson could be in line for another career day, and the only thing that may hold him back is a big lead that gets Jadyn Ott into the game. Arizona is ranked 28th in rushing defense. With the offensive line being tinkered with , I expect Patrick Mahomes to experiment with his receiving corps as well. It will be interesting to see whether Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen get a large uptick in snaps, but I am not sure it matters. Any receiver on the depth chart could have a big day against this defense. The Cardinals' offense is as limited as it gets. Trey McBride is their only real weapon, with a wide receiver group where not a single one has topped 100 yards total on the season. Running back Tyler Allgeier is a competent runner but doesn't threaten a defense. Lastly, Josh Johnson, a 19-year veteran journeyman, is under center for a team already on its fourth quarterback. Steve Spagnuolo's key will be limiting McBride, and with the Chiefs' cornerbacks holding down the outside, they should be able to do that. away.headline: Carson Beck Injured, Latest Updates on Cardinals QB's Status vs. Chiefs for NFL Week 11
away.blurb: Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday because of back spasms. On Friday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Friday he was preparing to start Johnson after Beck did not practice due to a back injury. After not being listed on the injury report Wednesday, Beck was added on Thursday, as he was a limited participant in practice. The third-round pick out of Miami struggled to get much going in a 34-6 loss to the Rams, completing 11 of his 18 passing attempts for 108 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions, while also getting sacked five times. The Arizona Cardinals will turn to veteran backup quarterback Josh Johnson when they face the Kansas City Chiefs. After the Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending UCL injury, Beck made his first career NFL start against the Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday. Arizona signed Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad following the Minshew injury, and he may now be in line to start just a couple of weeks later. Johnson, 40, has spent time with numerous teams over the course of his lengthy NFL career, and the Cardinals could become the eighth different team with which he has seen regular-season action. Over 50 career NFL games, including 11 starts, Johnson is 2-9, and he has completed 58.7 percent of his passing attempts for 2,669 yards, 14 touchdowns and 18 interceptions. Johnson made two starts for the Washington Commanders last season, posting a 1-1 record. Even with Beck in the lineup, the 3-7 Cardinals were going to be massive underdogs on the road against a 7-2 Chiefs team that is battling with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West lead.

away.headline: Cardinals get bad news on Carson Beck’s status for Week 11 amid back injury
away.blurb: Gardner Minshew, Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne, and Jeremiyah Love are all out for an extended period of time. Only Love might be back at some point this season. Carson Beck is throwing to a lackluster supporting cast. But now even he is banged up. Beck went on the injury report on Thursday with a back injury, putting his status for Week 11 in doubt. That doubt now appears to be close to a certainty, as the expectation is Beck will be ruled out for the Chiefs game. MORE : Grading NFL trade deadline debuts, from Kirk Cousins' Vikings return to Josh Downs' impressive day He's not yet ruled out, but Cardinals fans should anticipate missing out on Beck for Week 11 against the Chiefs, with a return in Week 12 or Week 13 against the Washington Commanders or Philadelphia Eagles more likely to be Beck's second NFL start. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' final injury report for Week 11 vs. Arizona Cardinals confirms the team will be shorthanded on offense
away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their final injury report ahead of Week 11's game against the Arizona Cardinals. After practice on Friday, Chiefs HC Andy Reid confirmed a third straight missed practice for three players on the offensive side of the ball. “The guys who didn't practice today were Jaylon Moore, Trey Smith, and Ken Walker,” Reid said. “All of which are improving.” Reid said all three players would likely be ruled out for the game. The decision on Walker was expected after NFL Insiders reported earlier this week that Kansas City could sit him for a second game. Emmett Johnson is expected to get his second career start on Sunday. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related It looks like it'll be another week for Chiefs DT Omarr Norman-Lott, who continues to work his way back from his 2025 knee injury. He was activated to the 53-man roster earlier this week . He's been limited in every practice session since the team opened his 21-day practice window. DT Peter Woods was downgraded to limited participation during Friday's practice session. He has missed the past two games with his neck injury. away.headline: Cardinals-Chiefs Injury Report Keeps Door Open For Carson Beck
away.blurb: "Carson will be DNP today. Not going to shut the door on him, but we're going to proceed as if Josh [Johnson] is going to be starting on Sunday," LaFleur told reporters on Friday. The Cardinals stuck true to their word, as Beck was listed as questionable on the team's official Friday injury report. OUT - Zach Carter (knee), Jon Gaines (ankle) QUESTIONABLE - Carson Beck (back) Carter remains out while working through his 21-day practice window in his return from injured reserve while Gaines practiced Wednesday but not Thursday/Friday before being ruled out. Beck carried no injury designation after his rookie debut, practiced fine on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday, which raised some concerns. OUT - Jaylon Moore (ankle), Trey Smith (concussion), Kenneth Walker (groin) QUESTIONABLE - Omarr Norman-Lott (knee), Peter Woods (neck) None of Kansas City's three players marked out practiced in any capacity this week while both Norman-Lott and Woods hit the field for all three days in some capacity. Cardinals-Chiefs Injury Report Keeps Door Open For Carson Beck Skip to main content SI.COM ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are holding on to hope. Carson Beck is not expected to be the team's starting quarterback when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11 thanks to a back injury that popped up this week. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said the team isn't closing the door on Beck playing Sunday, though they're preparing for their fourth starting quarterback in as many weeks with Josh Johnson now expected to be under center. The picture for both sides entering Week 11: Arizona Cardinals Injury Report Now, barring an eye-opening turnaround, Beck is set to be sidelined. Kansas City Chiefs Injury Report This is the second time Beck suffered a back injury, as earlier in the regular season the rookie quarterback was listed on Arizona's injury report with the same issue that's now flaring up once again. "I can't answer that because you just treat it," LaFleur told reporters when asked if there's anything that the Cardinals can do for Beck's back injury. "You go with the people that know what they're doing to treat it, and it's not like it's the first time he's dealt with it. So he's going about his business. He's going to handle it just like he does preparing for a football game, just like he does playing a football game. So we'll see. We'll see more tomorrow." Official game inactives are due 90 minutes before kickoff in Arrowhead, and it seems like the Cardinals are wanting to keep the door open down to the wire. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' second injury report for Week 11 tilt vs. Arizona Cardinals shows an important upgrade on defense
home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their second injury report ahead of Week 11's game against the Arizona Cardinals. The Chiefs' injury report looked mostly the same on Wednesday . That isn't exactly good news for guys like Jaylon Moore, Kenneth Walker, and Trey Smith. However, the team had one player with his practice status upgraded on defense. Nick Bolton dealt with a shin contusion and was limited during Wednesday's first practice session. The defensive leader fully participated in practice on Thursday. Here’s a quick breakdown of each team’s Week 11 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. The team will release game status designations Friday, Nov. 20. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related Don't expect to see DT Omarr Norman-Lott back in action this week as he continues to ramp up in his return from injury. Here's what Steve Spagnuolo had to say about ONL today: “We'll see where he is. He's kind of working through the injury. I think the training staff's done a great job with him. Now it's kind of getting acclimated back to the hard thing when you come off of this in the middle of the season. You know, you don't have the luxury of training camp with pads, and so we'll have to see where we're at.” Carson Beck was added to the injury report on Thursday with a back injury. This sounds more like a planned limited practice session with a nagging injury than something that could keep him out of Week 11's game. Here's what Steve Spagnuolo said about Beck on Thursday: “I'll be honest with you, we've obviously gone back and watched Miami tape. You know, you look at the quarterback you're going to play. This guy doesn't look like a rookie, in my opinion. (Carson) Beck, right? And if you look at that first drive last week, he's boom, boom. He had one that he put right on the tight end, and the tight end dropped it. Had they caught that, they might have, you know, been right down in the end zone. I didn't see him wilt at all. He stands up in there big. I see some throws. I'm looking for happy feet, but I don't see that. I mean, I think this guy's got pretty good control. I know he's played a lot of football, won a lot of games in college. He's a winner.” Jon Gaines was the only other Cardinals player downgraded on Thursday. He went from limited participation to a non-participant. He's missed some time for Arizona and could be another week before he's ready. Kansas City Chiefs WR Josh Downs found the end zone in his Week 10 debut against the Atlanta Falcons. When QB Patrick Mahomes discussed what stood out, he pointed somewhere else entirely. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. Eagles Get Brutal Injury News on All-Pro Defender During Steelers Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Eagles Get Brutal Injury News on All-Pro Defender During Steelers Matchup The Philadelphia Eagles are attempting to put the finishing touches on an improbable victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 11, as they have comfortably led against the AFC North contender for much of the day. Once this game wraps up, though, the Eagles are going to have to quickly turn their attention to Week 12, as they play the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day. A lot has gone right for the Eagles on Sunday, but they have a new problem that has emerged from this game involving All-Pro cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. During this game, Mitchell suffered a hamstring injury, and late in the fourth quarter, Philly announced a crushing update on his status that could have a big impact on the team moving forward. All year long, the Eagles have been hit hard by the injury bug, as evidenced by the fact that another pair of players, linebacker Zack Baun and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks, were placed on injured reserve ahead of this game. A handful of stars are still kicking around, trying to help Philly win games, with Mitchell being one of them. After earning Pro Bowl and All-Pro First Team honors last year, Mitchell has clearly established himself as one of the better cornerbacks in the NFL. While it's been a rough season as a whole for Philadelphia, Mitchell has maintained his high level of play, as he has 40 tackles, one interception, and nine pass breakups to his name this year.
