home.headline: Steelers Get Concerning Injury News on Star Pass Rusher During Eagles Clash
home.blurb: Shortly after his second sack, though, Highsmith went down with an ankle injury, which immediately raised concern among the team and its fans. As of right now, Highsmith's status is up in the air, as the team officially ruled him questionable to return to the game as a result of this new ankle ailment. "Steelers LB Alex Highsmith (ankle) is questionable to return. Already has two sacks today," Mike Garafolo of NFL Network shared in a post on X. With Herbig being ruled out for this game before kickoff, Highsmith's absence looms even larger for the Steelers, which means Watt is going to have to step up and try to take over the game on his own in order to prevent things from getting out of hand. Folks will have to keep their eyes peeled for a more concrete update on Highsmith, but right now, things aren't looking great for him when it comes to his injury status. The Pittsburgh Steelers have found themselves in a tough spot early in Week 11 , as they are in a 13-0 hole against a Philadelphia Eagles team that is being led by its third-string quarterback. Making matters even worse, the Steelers may be forced to get through the rest of this game without star pass rusher Alex Highsmith . It had been a big start to the day for Highsmith, as he picked up a pair of sacks in the first quarter as Pittsburgh excelled at creating pressure against Philadelphia's offense. However, he suffered an ankle injury shortly thereafter, with the team issuing an announcement on his status for the rest of the game. Alex Highsmith Suffers Ankle Injury vs. Eagles With Pittsburgh's offense laboring through the first half of the season, the defense has been forced to step up in an effort to lead the team to wins. Easily the best part of the Steelers' defense is its front seven, where Highsmith teams up with guys like T.J. Watt, Nick Herbig, and Cameron Heyward to consistently make the lives of opposing offensive linemen difficult. Of this group, Highsmith is more of a pass-rush specialist, having racked up at least six sacks in each of the past five seasons. He took a big step towards hitting that mark again on Sunday, as Highsmith dropped Joe Milton III twice in the backfield early in this game to increase his sack tally to 5.5 for the year. Steelers Bad Day Gets Even Worse With Alex Highsmith News The Steelers were widely expected to be able to find a way to beat the Eagles on Sunday, considering all the attrition the team is currently dealing with in the injury department, but things have not gone as expected to begin this game. Now, they could be without Highsmith for the rest of the game, which could make life even more difficult for Pittsburgh as it attempts to work its way back into this contest. home.headline: Steelers vs. Eagles Injury Report
home.blurb: Wide receiver DeVonta Smith is good to go for Sunday's game against the Steelers, but Dontayvion Wicks remains out. The Eagles are healthier coming out of the bye week and will welcome the return of wide receiver DeVonta Smith to the lineup on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, the Eagles will be without Smith's positionmate Dontayvion Wicks for the fourth game in a row. Wicks was limited in practice all week with an ankle injury. The team added a foot injury for Wicks on Friday's report. Linebacker Smael Mondon is doubtful for Sunday's game after missing the past two practices with an ankle injury. Running back Will Shipley did not practice on Friday due to an illness. He is questionable as he remains on Injured Reserve with a foot injury. He would need to be activated off Injured Reserve to the 53-man roster by 4 PM on Saturday to be eligible to play against the Steelers. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell is set to return to the lineup and start alongside Jeremiah Trotter Jr. with Baun out and Mondon doubtful. Campbell missed the past two games with hamstring and quad injuries. Defensive back Michael Carter missed three of the last four games with an abdomen injury. Wide receiver Britain Covey was out for the last two games with a knee injury. Cornerback Jonathan Jones is healthy after missing the past two games with a hamstring injury. The Steelers listed six players as questionable, including outside linebacker Nick Herbig, who suffered injuries to his hip and ribs last Sunday night in Cincinnati. Herbig did not practice all week. Three of the players who are questionable – guard Gennings Dunker, wide receiver Michael Pittman, and wide receiver Roman Wilson – are on Injured Reserve and, like Shipley for the Eagles, would need to be activated in order to play against Philadelphia. Wide receiver DeVonta Smith was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday after practicing in a limited capacity Wednesday. Smith told reporters after Wednesday's practice that he was back to 100 percent after missing five of the last six games with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Smael Mondon joined fellow linebacker Zack Baun on the sideline Thursday. Mondon was a full participant with an ankle injury on Wednesday, but did not participate in practice Thursday. Mondon stepped in during the Week 9 game against the Giants before the bye week after Baun suffered a back injury and Jihaad Campbell was out with hamstring and quad injuries. Baun has yet to practice this week, while Campbell is on track to return. Running back Will Shipley, practicing for the first time since the Week 5 game in London, was limited for the second straight day. The Eagles would need to activate him off of Injured Reserve to be eligible for Sunday's game. RB Will Shipley and WR Dontayvion Wicks spotted! away.headline: Ravens injury report: Madubuike misses practice; rookie Randall gearing up
away.blurb: With Madubuike, coach Jesse Minter said the team would see how his hamstring responds throughout the week before determining his availability Sunday afternoon in Carolina. This is an independent injury from the neck issue which shut down nearly all of the two-time All-Pro’s 2025 season. Should he be ruled out Sunday, that would leave Baltimore’s interior defensive line without its top performer. Rookie right guard Vega Ioane, who was limited Wednesday with a lingering shoulder injury, was a full participant Thursday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remains limited. He suffered a knee injury in Week 6 and has not played since. Minter insinuated he had a chance to play Monday night, but Hawkins was ultimately ruled out. Friday should bring more clarity on his status for Sunday’s game. Running back Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) is gearing up for his regular season NFL debut. The fifth-round rookie was activated off injured reserve on Wednesday and is pacing toward a full week of practice. Special teams coordinator Anthony Levine Sr. indicated Randall could be an immediate help in the return game. “He goes out there, and he works hard,” Levine said. “He catches the ball well. He has great coordination. He’s strong. He can run. He has great vision. So, I think he could help us in the return game. He could help us even in coverage, because the kid can run. Again, he’s physical. He has long arms. He knows how to get off blocks, and the most important thing is that he has the ‘want to.’ Panthers tight ends Darren Waller (knee) and Tommy Tremble (knee) both missed Wednesday’s practice but returned for Thursday’s session in a limited capacity. The same goes for running back Chuba Hubbard (rest). Fifty-one of the 53 players on the Ravens’ active roster were accounted for during Thursday’s practice. The only absences were defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike , who left Monday’s loss with a hamstring injury and has since missed consecutive practices, and cornerback Marlon Humphrey, who was sent home for disciplinary reasons . “He wants to get better, so he talks to me after practice. He talks to me before practice. He was just talking to me in the walk-through. So, I think it’ll be good for him. I think he can help us a lot.” On the other side, Carolina has a deceivingly long injury report. Thirteen players are listed. A closer inspection shows all but four fully participated Thursday. Only two haven’t practiced this week: Linebackers Bobby Okereke (foot) and Isaiah Simmons (knee). Running back Jonathon Brooks (groin), offensive lineman Brady Christensen (hamstring) and cornerback Mike Jackson (groin) are all practicing this week but remain on injured reserve. Have a news tip? Lamar Jackson Injury: Will Ravens’ Starting QB Return This Season? He wasn’t the only Raven to get hurt. Russell Street Report noted before the game that he had just one pressure in his previous two games after a solid run of 15 pressures in his first five games back from the finger injury. For a player the Ravens brought in to fix their pass rush, that’s a steep drop. The 4-7 Ravens have lost six straight and visit Houston on Sunday before their Week 13 bye. New York started off the season with a win in Tennessee and then beat Cleveland a few weeks later, but the Jets have since lost five in a row. On the flip side, the Chargers just picked up their first win of the season last week, upsetting the Ravens in Baltimore on Monday Night Football by a final score of 23-20. Los Angeles has won the last five meetings against the Jets, most recently picking up a 27-6 victory on the road in 2023. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 11 matchup with a final score prediction. Jets vs. Chargers Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Jets +3 (-112) Chargers -3 (-108) Chargers: -162 41.5 (Over -112/Under -108) Line Movement: The point spread hasn’t moved since the odds opened for this game, but the total is now at 41.5 after opening at 40.5. Jets vs. Chargers Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: Jets vs. Chargers Prediction I wrote last week that I can't quit on this Jets team, and I'm still convinced they're better than their record suggests. I used that logic to bet against them in a game against the Bills, which was a bet that didn't come close to cashing. Do you think I learned from my mistake? I haven't. I'm back on New York again this week against the Chargers. The Jets are 16th in the NFL in net yards per play, and their offense is 18th in EPA per play and 10th in success rate. Those aren't the numbers of a team that deserves to have a 2-8 record and are underdogs of a field goal against a bad Chargers team. I'll fall for this trap once more. Pick: Jets +3 (-115) via DraftKings The Jets trap has been an easy one to fall into, to be fair, but I’ll once again back New York alongside MacMillan here. Maybe the Chargers are feeling good and can ride the momentum of a win to put something together here. But that’s a risk I’m willing to take given the overall body of work of these two teams. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Sat, November 21, 2026 at 5:19 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets are on the road in Los Angeles, California to take on the Los Angeles Chargers in the Jets' 11th game of the 2026 season this Sunday. The Jets will be looking to get back on the winning track after dropping eight of their last nine games. These two teams last met in a 27 – 6 Chargers victory in 2023. The Chargers have won five straight against the Jets and seven of the last nine. The Chargers lead the overall series 24 – 14 – 1. The Chargers come into this game fresh off their first victory of the season, a 23 – 20 squeaker over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football. The Chargers are one of three one win teams in the NFL this season, along with the Miami Dolphins and the Tennessee Titans. They have been weighed down by atrocious quarterback play from the usually reliable Justin Herbert. Herbert has not meshed with the offense brought in by Mike McDaniel. The Chargers rank last in the NFL in points scored, last in the NFL in offensive turnovers, and bottom five in passing yards, passing touchdowns and interceptions. It has been a rough year for the Chargers offense, but they have had some success running the ball, ranking 10th in the NFL in rushing yards. On defense the Chargers have struggled against the pass while doing a decent job against the run. Let's make a few predictions for the game on Sunday. Omarion Hampton rushes for 90+ yards and a touchdown against a Jets defense that struggles mightily against the run. Justin Herbert is held under 200 yards passing. The Jets sack Herbert 4+ times and force at least one Herbert turnover. Geno Smith puts up 250+ passing yards and 2+ touchdowns. The Jets beat the Chargers in a tight game, the victory sealed by a late Chargers turnover. These predictions are just for fun. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jeremy Brener · SB Nation Tue, November 17, 2026 at 8:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Chargers are 1-8 after beating the Baltimore Ravens on the road in Week 10. Now the Chargers will have a chance to face off against the New York Jets at home in Week 11. The Jets are fresh off a loss against the Buffalo Bills at home, where Gino Smith exited the game and was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik. Smith hurt his ankle against the Bills, which puts his status for the game in jeopardy. The Bolts entered this week as 2.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 40.5 points. The Chargers picked up their first win of the season in a 23-20 victory on the road against the Ravens. Justin Herbert got things started with a 22-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter. Omarion Hampton also found the end zone in the second quarter. While the Ravens attempted to tighten the gap late with a 1-yard touchdown run from Derrick Henry, they were unable to complete the comeback, which gave the Chargers their first win of the season. Klubnik made his professional debut against Buffalo and completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards with an interception. He also ran three times for 26 yards. Glenn praised the rookie’s mobility Wednesday and said he would continue getting practice opportunities against the first- and second-team defenses. He played 37 snaps in relief of Smith. Running back Breece Hall came away encouraged by how Klubnik handled the huddle. away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 10:59 AM . Tight end Caleb Lohner's 21-day window opened this week in practice, and there is no rush for Denver to necessarily bring him onto the active roster right away, which leaves his official status as out for Sunday's game by default. away.headline: Injury Report: S Talanoa Hufanga among Broncos not assigned game statuses, S Brandon Jones questionable for Week 11 vs. Raiders
away.blurb: Injury Report: S Talanoa Hufanga among Broncos not assigned game statuses, S Brandon Jones questionable for Week 11 vs. Raiders Skip to main content Primary nav Game Day ENGLEWOOD, Colo. — Multiple Broncos appear poised to make their return to game action in Week 11 against the Las Vegas Raiders. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (concussion) and cornerback Riley Moss (concussion) were among Denver's players who were not assigned game statuses on the Broncos' final practice report of the week, which indicates they will be available to play. All three players were full participants throughout the week. Waddle and Moss, who suffered their respective injuries against the Panthers in Week 9, will also be set to return to the field. Moss signed a four-year contract extension on Thursday. Safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) was the lone Broncos player listed as questionable. Jones, who exited Denver's Week 8 win over Kansas City with his injury, was a limited participant in all three practices ahead of Week 11. Tight end Caleb Lohner (foot) was a full participant in all three practices as he returned to practice this week, but he was ruled out for Sunday's game. Jones, who was listed as questionable after he was a limited participant in all three practices ahead of Week 11, was among the team's inactive players. Hufanga appears set to play for the first time since suffering his injury in Week 5 against the Chargers. Similarly, the Giants don't need to be told they're good, too. They do, after all, lead the NFC East, despite criticisms that the division is weak sauce. They are the only team in the division with a positive point differential (+7). They are also pretty angry about having blown a chance against the Washington Commanders last week, a loss that gives the third-place Commanders the head-to-head tiebreaker if the two teams somehow end up with the same win-loss record at the end of the season. All of these factors have some critics snickering about the Giants' current standing. After all, someone has to be in first place, regardless of the division, right? And it's not that the Giants care what those outside of 1925 Giants Drive think about their team. Still, they can certainly make a statement with a convincing upset win over the Jaguars, who, surprisingly, FanDuel Sportsbook lists as only a 5.5-point favorite over Big Blue. Will the Giants come through and get their first home win since a 36-24 triumph over the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 4, 2026? Let's dive in. Why the Giants Will Win The easiest way for the Giants to win this game is to keep the Jaguars offense off the field. And it just so happens that the Giants are currently second in the league in average time of possession (32:26), behind the league-leading Chicago Bears (34:31). That's not bad considering the Giants' rushing game ranks 18th in the league (112.6 yards per game). Big Blue averages 5.7 plays per drive, tying it for seventh in the league (Jacksonville averages 5.8 plays per drive, for those wondering). In a nutshell, winning the time-of-possession battle will be key for the Giants if they want to secure a win. The Giants have leaned into their running game far more than they have in the past, and rain or no rain, that's not expected to change this week. Defensively, the Giants have been strong against the deep ball, which just so happens to be Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence's superpower. Lawrence has a 51.6 percent completion rate on passes of 20-plus air yards this season, fifth in the league. The Giants have a 38.4 percent blitz rate this season, fourth in the league, and have blitzed on 50 percent or more of their plays since Week 4, a 20 percent increase from the first three weeks. In terms of coverage, the Giants lead the league with a 17.2 percent completion rate allowed on deep balls of 20-plus air yards. They are also the only team not to allow a touchdown on a deep pass attempt, and they have four interceptions on those passes, tied for second in the league. Why the Giants Won't Beat the Jaguars Two potential reasons could doom the Giants' chances of scoring their first home win in over a month. The first is turnovers. The opportunistic Jaguars lead the league with a +9 turnover differential, having 16 takeaways to only seven giveaways. The Jaguars' takeaways include 12 interceptions ( fourth in the league ). The Giants currently have a -2 turnover differential, 21st in the league. They have three giveaways in their last three games (one interception and two lost fumbles). Fumbling has been an issue for the Giants, who have had six fumbles in their last two games. That's not good against an opportunistic Jacksonville team that is averaging 2.3 takeaways over its last three games. Give the Jaguars a short field to work with, and that's asking for trouble. The other thing to watch is the Jaguars' first-half scoring. The Jaguars lead the league in first-half scoring, averaging 15.89 points within the first 30 minutes of regulation. The Giants, meanwhile, have averaged 9.44 points per game in the first half. Needless to say, the Giants do not want to get into a situation where, late in the third or early in the fourth quarter, the Jaguars are so far ahead that Lawrence and other key starters get the rest of the afternoon off. They know that," Coen said on Friday. "I think they're a little bit ticked, especially on the defensive side from some of the things that happened on Sunday that wasn't up to our standard. So, I think when you have a hungry group that feels as if they have not done anything yet. Nothing. We're in the second half of the season. A lot to prove, a lot of work, more games to be played than we even just did and went through. We have new additions now where this is our football team. This is an opportunity as we move forward throughout these next few weeks to go and put it on tape with this team, our final football team of who we are for the rest of the season. Let's go put together four quarters of our best because we have yet to do it yet.” So, how do the national predictions see this one playing out as the Jaguars make a push in the AFC? We take a look below. ESPN's Seth Wickersham is picking against the Jaguars for a second week in a row after, for some reason, picking the Tennessee Titans last week . I respect a good bit when I see it, and that is quite the bit. But as a whole, the Jaguars are the favorites because they are simply one of the best teams in the entire NFL. The Giants have been better than expected this season, though their wins have come against teams with losing records, and they are 0-1-1 against the powerhouse that is the 2026 Washington Commanders. They are a solid team, but the Jaguars have been on a different tier this season. The Jaguars enter Week 11 as the only team that ranks top-5 in both points per game (29.9, 4th) and points per game allowed (16.0, 2nd), leading the NFL with a +125 point differential. Jacksonville's point differential through nine games is the franchise's best since 1999 (+137). The Jaguars are 7-2 or better through nine games for the third time in franchise history, joining 1998 and 1999, the only seasons they won consecutive division titles. Offensively, the Jaguars will have to find a way to beat the blitz as the Giants send pressure at some of the highest rates in the entire NFL. The Jaguars' offense has hit big plays against the blitz this season, but they have not been as effecient down-to-down as they have when defenses are just sending four pass-rushers. Defensively, the Jaguars will need their new defensive pieces to make an impact. Jessie Bates III is set to start at safety and Jordan Davis is set to start at nose tackle, with each player set to potentially give the Jaguars a boost. Bates can help the Jaguars with turnovers and limiting big plays, while the Jaguars will need Davis right off the bat to make an impact against the Giants' running game. The Giants should give the Jaguars more of a test than most teams have had in recent weeks, but I still got the Jaguars in this one. Jaguars 27, Giants 17. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Vikings-49ers live updates Tarik Skubal to Mets NFL Week 11 Winners-Losers Tom Jackson dies College football winners/losers NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.

away.headline: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
away.blurb: The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected. But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus. The Jaguars also had the following players listed as limited on Thursday: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box. Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday. “Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways." The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room. This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 11 picks, including the Jaguars to handle the Giants on the road Imagn Images Stacking winning weeks is always a good feeling when it comes to picking NFL games . I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Pick: Bengals 34, Commanders 30 Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. San Francisco enters this game with the best record in the NFC at 8-1, and Brock Purdy and company have the No. 1 offense in the NFL in EPA/Play this season. Kyle Shanahan's team is coming off a 46-point showing in a win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 10, and it's favored in this neutral-site game that could end up deciding the No. 1 seed in the conference. Meanwhile, the Vikings have seen their Super Bowl odds skyrocket since trading for Kirk Cousins at the deadline, as Minnesota upset the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in Week 10. The Vikings started the season 6-0, but back-to-back losses to Detroit and Buffalo forced the team to make a move to upgrade at quarterback. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz struggled to open this season, but Cousins, who knows this offense and scheme, has already made a major upgrade to this passing game. Will that be enough for the Vikings to get an upset win over another Super Bowl contender? Oddsmakers are giving the 49ers the edge, but Minnesota has seen its odds improve across the board since the Cousins deal. The Vikings' defense is one of the three best in the league in EPA/Play and has been dominant with blitzes all season long. This should be a fun chess match between Shanahan and Brian Flores, as they're two of the best play-calling minds in the league. I've compiled some of our favorites all in one spot to help you bet on this NFC showdown. This week, he’s targeting the Vikings to cover in this NFC showdown: I was waiting all season to fade the Minnesota Vikings, but they went out and got Kirk Cousins, and now their only weakness has been addressed. Cousins isn't a top-10 quarterback this season, but he's certainly good enough that the Vikings can win based on their defense and the rest of their offensive weapons. Cousins immediately and seamlessly slid into their offense this past week, and all of a sudden the Vikings look like a Super Bowl contender. The 49ers are the clear top team in the NFC, but this is going to be one of their toughest challenges this season. They have enjoyed playing the fifth-easiest schedule so far this season, and now they face a defense that's going to make them pay for the plethora of injuries they have, especially on offense. I'll take the field goal with the Vikings in what I expect will be a game that comes down to the wire. Jefferson has seen his value skyrocket since the team traded for Cousins. The superstar receiver was targeted a season-high 13 times in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Green Bay Packers, reeling in nine passes for 74 yards. While he didn’t find the end zone, Jefferson has received nine or more targets in each of the last three weeks. So, Kevin O’Connell and the Vikings are making a point of getting their top receiver involved as they look to win the NFC North. Jefferson has had a down season by his standards, yet he’s still found the end zone four times. San Francisco allowed four scores to the Cowboys’ top two receivers in Week 10 (three to George Pickens and one to CeeDee Lamb), and the team has allowed the 12th-most passing scores in the NFL. The 49ers are just 16th in the league in EPA/Pass, and there’s no doubt that Cousins has elevated this Vikings offense. Jefferson and Cousins have a ton of chemistry from earlier in Kirk’s career, and I think the star wideout will turn his massive target share into a touchdown in Week 11. MacMillan also shared his favorite props for the week in his Player Prop Countdown , and he’s fading Purdy in the deep passing game on Sunday: We all know the Vikings' defense is elite, but one of their biggest strengths is not allowing explosive plays. They have allowed just 19 completions of 20+ yards and only five completions of 40+ yards this season. This could also be a great opportunity to fade Brock Purdy, who has benefited from facing some weak secondaries this season. His injured receiving corps could come back to haunt him this week when he has to take on the best defense in football. I expect Kyle Shanahan to lean on short completions to the likes of George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey to help Purdy deal with Brian Flores' blitzing defense. If that happens, I foresee a scenario where he doesn't complete an explosive play as he did at all last week against the Cowboys. 49ers wideout Deebo Samuel Sr. has appeared in six games this season, finding the end zone five times. Deebo is a bit of a matchup anomaly, as he’s going to work as both a pass catcher and a rusher in the San Fran offense and is coming off a two-score game against Dallas in Week 10. The Minnesota defense is a much tougher matchup, but Deebo gets plenty of touches on misdirection that have led to some big plays. He’s averaging 12.5 yards per reception and 13 yards per carry in the 2026 season. At +235, I think the veteran receiver is a little undervalued considering the fact that he’s scored in four of his six appearances (he was injured in one that he failed to score) this season. picks.headline: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers in Mexico City
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers in Mexico City Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Even if you’re not a fan of the Vikings or 49ers, Sunday night’s primetime match in Mexico City is the definition of a “must-watch.” Two of the best teams in the NFL colliding on the international stage, with playoff seeding and bragging rights on the line, is everything the NFL dreamed of when it set the 2026 schedule last spring. The stakes could not be much higher for a late-November game, and I expect both teams to put on a show. With a newfound Kirk Cousins-sized confidence boost in Minnesota , the Vikings should be set up well to meet the moment. Here are three things I see happening Sunday night at Estadio Banorte. 1. Vikings' defense slows down 49ers' attack The 49ers have been one of the most balanced offenses in the NFL, averaging a league-high 399.8 yards per game. They’re averaging the seventh-most passing yards per game at 255.8 and the third-most rushing yards per game at 144. San Francisco is also second in the league with 31.2 points per game. Simply put, the 49ers' offense can move the ball any way it needs to. The Minnesota Vikings defense ranks 1st in dropback success rate allowed, per @SumerSports The San Francisco 49ers offense ranks 1st in dropback success rate and has the highest dropback success rate of any team through 10 weeks since the 2018 Saints The Vikings' defense, on the other hand, has allowed the fewest points (14) and the second-fewest yards (236.1) per game to opposing offenses. They’ve also held their own against some of the league's best offenses, holding Detroit, Buffalo, and Green Bay to 19, 23, and 10 points over the last few weeks. Now that they have a dependable QB to keep the offense on the field, they’ll be able to catch their breath in the high altitude of Mexico City. Minnesota's defense will need all hands on deck to slow down an elite offense, but Brian Flores will certainly have his unit ready. Give me the Vikings defense to hold the 49ers under 330 total yards and 24 points. 2. Jauan Jennings finds the end zone The Vikings signed Jauan Jennings this past May for two main reasons: to open up the run game as a blocker and to be a reliable third wide receiver after Jalen Nailor’s departure in free agency. So far, neither has materialized the way head coach Kevin O’Connell and interim general manager Rob Brzezinski had hoped. Jennings has also missed the Vikings’ past two games with a calf injury, after previously missing Week 2 to attend to a personal family matter. Now, with Jennings set to return against his former team and WR2 Jordan Addison missing time, the former 49er has his chance to shine . Jennings’s struggles this season have largely been due to poor quarterbacking. The 29-year-old has certainly been open, and Cousins may be the perfect passer to actually get him the ball. I predict that Jennings finds new life and scores at least one touchdown against his former team on Sunday night. 3. Sunday's matchup is only the beginning of what's to come This may already be the NFL’s game of the year. The well-balanced 49ers against the blitz-happy Vikings is a matchup made for the primetime stage. But who says this has to be their only meeting? away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. We’ll see. Kyle Shanahan says they’ll see how he does in a Saturday walk-through before deciding on whether he’ll play on Sunday night or not. Dre Greenlaw is dealing with a neck injury and his been limited in the last two practices after missing the first one this week. Kyle Shanahan said that neck/nerve injuries can be difficult to predict, but he’s heading in the right direction. That’s another one that while questionable (which means more likely to play in reality) may be closer to a 50/50 chance. He would be a significant loss if he couldn’t go on Sunday night. Upton Stout is their slot corner and has been limited all week with shoulder/neck injuries and is also questionable. This is reportedly an AC joint issue that he has been playing through since he suffered it early in October so it would seem more likely he continue to play through it on Sunday night, although it has affected his performance. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, it looks like just Jordan Addison and Kyler Murray will be out for Sunday's game. Addison just had thumb surgery and won't play on Sunday while Murray won't be active either with his hamstring injury. For the 49ers, beyond the IR players both Mike Evans and Dre Greenlaw didn't practice today (although Evans was seen doing a few very limited things on a side field). 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said he hoped Evans would practice later this week and hoped he could go on Sunday. For now he looks more doubtful but we'll see how he progresses during the week. Getting him back would be big for the 49ers offense. Brock Purdy's EPA/dropback has been roughly twice as high with Evans in the lineup than without. Evans has missed the last three Niners' games with Achilles tendonitis. Renardo Green is also one to keep an eye on as a starting cornerback. He has been dealing with a back injury for a couple weeks now and had to leave the Cowboys game on Sunday because of it. We'll see how it goes with him and Stout- another cornerback limited to start the week. My guess is that Green will be questionable on Sunday and if he plays he won't be 100%. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Commanders odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 11 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Vikings-49ers live updates Tarik Skubal to Mets NFL Week 11 Winners-Losers Tom Jackson dies College football winners/losers Patrick Judis · SB Nation Fri, November 20, 2026 at 11:30 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cincinnati Bengals have been one of the hottest teams in the NFL and are tied with a handful of teams with a five-game win streak. That culminated in an absolute whooping of the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Sunday Night Football that wasn't even as close as the 20-point win made it seem. Now they are taking their show on the road to play the Washington Commanders in their house on Monday Night Football. Joe Burrow is 0-2 so far in his career against the Commanders, but that comes with some pretty big caveats. The first loss was the game in which he injured his knee midway through the game as a rookie. The other loss came in an absolute monster of a shootout where the Bengals defense did not stop the Commanders or Jayden Daniels a single time in 2024, with the game ending 38-33. That would not be the first time Burrow would helm a losing team despite putting up more than 30 points over the next few seasons. These teams are drastically different as the Cincinnati defense has had a major overhaul, and Washington is far from the team it was during Daniels' rookie season. There is no doubt Daniels is a talented quarterback, but the Commanders themselves seem to be a very average to below-average team that needs a combination of home run hits on offense and a handful of turnovers to spark a win. Meanwhile, Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are giving their best impressions of the Colts' offense during Peyton Manning's heyday by trusting their quarterback to put up points with his top weapons over a balanced attack. That has led to four straight games of four touchdowns for Burrow, which ties a record set by Manning. The real x-factor here will be the Bengals defense. Will the version we have seen since the Madrid game against the Atlanta Falcons show up that has been able to contain opposing offenses that tried to test their linebackers and safeties? Or will the young players at those positions allow a few too many big plays? Here is how the oddsmakers and experts feel about the game. The Bengals are currently 6.5-point road favorites against the Commanders, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . It really is a fairly big deal when a road team gets almost a touchdown advantage over a home team. It clearly shows that there is a step between where these two teams are currently at. The point total is set at 53.5 is the second highest of the week. That is fair because even when this team has faced teams like the Tennessee Titans, they have given up opportunities to score. 10 of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has all seven experts taking Cincinnati to win All five of NFL.com's experts are expecting the Bengals to extend their win streak to six games NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick I think this team has really turned a corner as far as this defense is concerned. The young linebacker duo of Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter have grown enough to prove to be a competent — maybe not the most consistent — duo. That is the level of play this defense needs when the defensive line led by Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence is able to get penetration. We will have to see how well they contain Daniels, who can really cause some damage by extending plays with his legs. All of that more or less will determine how much the Commanders lose by. Washington has no way of slowing down or throwing off this offense. The Bengals are getting into at least the 30s. Can the Commanders keep pace? Final Score: Bengals 45, Commanders 25 Who Dey! picks.headline: NFL analyst makes wild Commanders-Bengals Week 11 prediction
picks.blurb: NFL analyst makes wild Commanders-Bengals Week 11 prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Vikings-49ers live updates Tarik Skubal to Mets NFL Week 11 Winners-Losers Tom Jackson dies College football winners/losers NFL analyst makes wild Commanders-Bengals Week 11 prediction Bryan Manning, Commanders Wire · Commanders Wire Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:10 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When did the Washington Commanders last play the Cincinnati Bengals ? It was in Week 3 of the 2024 season—Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels' rookie season. The Commanders, led by a nearly perfect game from Daniels, shocked the Bengals on the road, 38-33. Daniels' late fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Terry McLaurin was one of the top plays of that season. On Monday, the Bengals meet the Commanders again in prime time. Cincinnati enters Monday night's game 7-2 and winners of five in a row. Quarterback Joe Burrow is playing at an MVP level, completing almost 75% of his passes, with 2,795 passing yards, 27 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's coming off a win over Pittsburgh, where he passed for 409 yards and four touchdowns. So, it's no surprise that the Bengals opened as solid 6.5-point favorites over the Commanders. Washington's record (3-5-1) may not show it, but the Commanders have been playing better football recently. Quarterback Jayden Daniels is quietly having an excellent bounce-back season, playing with a dislocated left elbow and dealing with numerous injuries around him. The Commanders' defense got off to a rough start under new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, but has looked like a different unit over the last few weeks. On Monday, they'll have their biggest test of the year, defending Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. While oddsmakers have the Bengals as favorites, so do NFL analysts. NFL.com analysts predicted the outcome of Monday's Week 11 game between the Commanders and Bengals. All 10 picks were in favor of Cincinnati. That's not really a surprise. However, one analyst predicted that the Bengals will defeat the Commanders 63-21. Cincinnati is certainly capable of putting up a lot of points against Washington. 63? Don't count on it. Head coach Dan Quinn should post that graphic in the Commanders' locker room for everyone to see this week. away.blurb: The Washington Commanders got some bad news at the end of Friday’s practice. Starting cornerback Amik Robertson suffered an ankle injury on the last day of practice. He did not practice on Saturday and the Commanders listed him as questionable on the final injury report for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals . Losing Robertson would be significant. He’s been Washington’s best and most consistent defensive back. His competitiveness sets the tone for the entire team. According to head coach Dan Quinn, Robertson could be a game-time decision on Monday. “So, yeah, [Amik’s injury] on the last play of the day [Friday], so it was sore today, so we held [him] out. I’ll monitor over the next, you know, 48 hours,” Quinn said. In some good news, no players were ruled out for Monday night’s game. However, three others were listed as questionable: Croskey-Merritt had his 21-day window opened last week. Quinn indicated on Saturday that things were trending positively for Washington’s starting running back to return on Monday. White has handled the bulk of running back duties while Croskey-Merritt is out, but Quinn seemed to indicate that he believed White could play against the Bengals. Finally, Patrick is listed as questionable, but practiced fully on Saturday and Quinn said he'd be back in the starting lineup. He suffered a concussion two weeks ago against the Rams and missed last week’s win over the Giants . Former starter Nick Allegretti played well in Patrick’s absence. home.headline: Commanders injury updates: Four questionable vs Bengals on Monday
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders got some bad news at the end of Friday’s practice. Starting cornerback Amik Robertson suffered an ankle injury on the last day of practice. He did not practice on Saturday and the Commanders listed him as questionable on the final injury report for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals . Losing Robertson would be significant. He’s been Washington’s best and most consistent defensive back. His competitiveness sets the tone for the entire team. According to head coach Dan Quinn, Robertson could be a game-time decision on Monday. “So, yeah, [Amik’s injury] on the last play of the day [Friday], so it was sore today, so we held [him] out. I’ll monitor over the next, you know, 48 hours,” Quinn said. In some good news, no players were ruled out for Monday night’s game. However, three others were listed as questionable: Croskey-Merritt had his 21-day window opened last week. Quinn indicated on Saturday that things were trending positively for Washington’s starting running back to return on Monday. White has handled the bulk of running back duties while Croskey-Merritt is out, but Quinn seemed to indicate that he believed White could play against the Bengals. Finally, Patrick is listed as questionable, but practiced fully on Saturday and Quinn said he'd be back in the starting lineup. He suffered a concussion two weeks ago against the Rams and missed last week’s win over the Giants . Former starter Nick Allegretti played well in Patrick’s absence. home.headline: Injury Report: Washington Commanders vs. Cincinnati Bengals
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders will enter week 11 with four players ruled questionable. The final injury report released on Saturday listed running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt, cornerback Amik Robertson, offensive lineman Lucas Patrick and running back Rachaad White as questionable, hours after head coach Dan Quinn expressed optimism surrounding the status of several players. That included Croskey-Merritt, who Quinn pointed to as trending in the right direction to make his first long-awaited return. Croskey-Merritt was sidelined in the week six loss against the San Francisco 49ers with a groin injury, but saw his 21 day practice window officially opened to begin the practice week. Quinn also confirmed that Patrick is set to return as the team's starting center prior to the injury report being released. Patrick was sidelined in the week ten win after remaining in concussion protocol, an injury suffered the week prior. Washington turned to Nick Allegretti as the starter in week ten after rookie Lucas Patrick replaced him in the second half against the Los Angeles Rams. The status of Croskey-Merritt looms large with uncertainty about White after being a limited participant on Friday before not suiting up for Saturday's practice. White was the one who primarily stepped up in the running back room to replace Croskey-Merritt's production, doing so efficiently after tallying one rushing touchdown and averaging nearly 4.5 yards per carry over his last three games. Head coach Dan Quinn ponted to the chance to sit White during practice in an effort to reduce the soreness as he battles through a heel injury. Cornerback Amik Robertson suffered an ankle injury on the final play of Friday's practice, leading him to become a limited participant during Saturday's practice. After pointing to the 48 hours ahead as a chance to evaluate his status ahead of kickoff, Quinn also pointed to Rasul Douglas and a combination of Mike Sainristil and Fabian Moreau inside to mitigate his absence. Yet the Bengals will also work through a notable injury in the trenches with starting right guard Dalton Risner ruled out due to a knee injury. He joins linebacker Oren Burks as inactives for Cincinnati. Meanwhile, safety Kyle Duggar, guard Dylan Fairchild, cornerback Daxton Hill and guard Brian Parker II have all been ruled questionable ahead of Monday night. home.blurb: Linebacker Oren Burks (groin) and right guard Dalton Risner (knee) were the other DNPs, as foretold by coach Zac Taylor prior to practice . Burks isn't expected to practice all week, while Risner is considered day-to-day. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) and left guard Dylan Fairchild (oblique) were each limited Thursday. Dugger has been week-to-week for the last few weeks as he's still dealing with an injury from all the way back in Week 3. Fairchild suffered his injury in Week 9 and was able to play most of last week despite it. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman (forearm) practice for the first time since Week 5 as he was designated to return off the Reserve/Injured list Thursday. Cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring), WR Andrei Iosivas (thumb), and G Brian Parker II (knee) remain full participants as they await activation to the 53-man roster . Quarterback Joe Burrow is one of a few Bengals dealing with an illness. Bengals' Thursday injury report for NFL Week 11 Joe Burrow isn't alone under the weather Quarterback Joe Burrow (illness) was a full participant at practice, but the club announced during practice he is dealing with an illness and would not speak with reporters after practice. Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase took Burrow's place at his post-practice presser. “I don't know if he told y'all how he's feeling or not, but overall he looks good,” Chase said of Burrow while wearing his orange No. 9 practice jersey. “I think everybody around the team is just coming on with a little sickness. But overall, he still looks good. Still feels the same.” He's not wrong. Starting cornerback Dax Hill and offensive tackle Myles Hinton are also dealing with illnesses. Hill wasn't able to practice at all. Hinton was a late add to last week's injury report with his illness and was a full participant Thursday. Burrow being able to practice fully Thursday is obviously good news for his prospects playing Monday. He's expected to address the media either Friday or Saturday. WR Tee Higgins (knee) and safety PJ Jules (ankle) were also full participants.
